strengths_deep_dive: Despite financial and operational limitations, the Institute for Understanding Anti-Palestinian Racism fills a distinct niche within the advocacy sector. In 2024, the charity published <cite id="2">preliminary survey findings documenting direct experiences of discrimination</cite> and its specific impacts on community health. Furthermore, it maintains open access to its work by providing <cite id="2">pro-bono webinars, myth-busting materials, and incident reporting tools</cite> to educate the public without charging fees.
rich_narrative.summary: The Institute for Understanding Anti-Palestinian Racism focuses on research and education but faces challenges with high overhead costs. In FY2024, the organization reported a <cite id="1">total revenue of $84,465</cite> to support its work in addressing anti-Palestinian discrimination. The charity operates several initiatives, including conducting empirical surveys, offering free webinars, producing educational resources, and tracking incident reports. A key highlight of its work is documenting how bias impacts individuals, backed by publication of <cite id="2">empirical research on health effects</cite>. However, significant financial constraints exist. In FY2024, the organization operated with a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 34.9%</cite>, which falls well short of the 75% industry standard and the <cite id="4">peer program ratio median of 79.4%</cite>. This indicates that over 65% of expenditures were directed toward non-program administrative overhead. Additionally, as a young entity founded in 2024, the charity has a limited operational track record and lacks comprehensive public financial disclosure, resulting in low data confidence. Contributions qualify as sadaqah or general charitable giving.
